title_en: Fragments on the Letter to the Ephesians
author: Severian of Gabala
occasion: Catenae excerpts preserving Severian's explanations of difficult points in Ephesians, especially the relationship of law and gospel, the divine plan, and the church as Christ's body.
argument: Severian reads Ephesians as Paul's timely instruction to believers already prepared by John's preaching, urging them not to be held fast by the law. He argues that Paul carefully distinguishes the Father and the Son while honoring both, and that Christ's incarnation recapitulated and reconciled all things. The law's dividing wall between Jews and Greeks was abolished not because the commandments were inappropriate but because their temporary custom was no longer useful. The church is the body of Christ and the fullness of God, and the Spirit intercedes for believers and enables spiritual requests free from fleshly elements.

outline.move: Introduces the occasion of Ephesians, Paul's apostolic authority, and the dignity of the incarnation, then comments on Ephesians 1:1–21.
Explains 'Father of glory' as referring to God's essence, discusses the names of heavenly powers, and comments on the church as Christ's body and the fullness of God through Ephesians 2:14–15a.
Continues on the dividing wall and the law of commandments, showing how Christ made peace and reconciled Jews and Greeks, through Ephesians 3:15.

Comments on the fatherhood of God, the dimensions of the cross, the church as God's fullness, spiritual gifts, redeeming the time, the Eucharist, marriage as a type of Christ and the church, and the Spirit's sword and prayer, through Ephesians 6:24.

cast.name: Paul
cast.who: The apostle and author of Ephesians, presented as writing with apostolic authority.

cast.name: John
cast.who: John the Evangelist, whose prior preaching in Ephesus prepared the believers.

cast.name: Christ
cast.who: The incarnate Son of God, through whom reconciliation and recapitulation are accomplished.

cast.name: Ezekiel
cast.who: Prophet cited as the first to call God's essence 'glory' in his vision.

cast.name: David
cast.who: Psalmist cited on God settling the solitary in a house.

cast.name: Adam
cast.who: First man, whose formation and union with Eve typify Christ and the church.

cast.name: Eve
cast.who: Taken from Adam's side, a type of the church formed from Christ.

voices.speaker: Paul (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Quotations from Ephesians introduced by lemmata (Eph 1,1 etc.); Paul is referred to in third person.

voices.speaker: Scripture (Old Testament)
voices.how_marked: Citations introduced by name (Ἰεζεκιὴλ, ∆αυίδ) or with ὁ θεός φησιν.

voices.speaker: The Lord (quoted)
voices.how_marked: One saying introduced with 'even if the Lord says' (κἂν ὁ κύριος λέγῃ).

key_terms.sense: God's saving plan, especially the incarnation of Christ
The Mosaic law, whose temporary customs are fulfilled and set aside in Christ
The dividing wall of the fence separating Jews from Greeks, abolished by Christ
Fullness; the church as the body of Christ filled with God
The church, the body of Christ and fullness of God
Christ's recapitulation or summing up of all things after the fall
Peace made by Christ between Jews and Greeks and between heaven and earth
Glory, used of God's essence and of the praise due to his grace
Grace, God's gift received through the Spirit, contrasted with law
The Holy Spirit, whose power enables prayer and whose sword is God's word
The body of Christ, identified with the church
A type or pattern, especially Adam and Eve's union as a type of Christ and the church
Redemption, the deliverance by which believers become God's possession
Adoption as sons, the status of the saints in Christ

scripture: Severian cites the Septuagint, using Greek book names and Psalm numbering. Modern citations should follow standard English Bible names and Hebrew Psalm numbering where they differ from the Septuagint.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is uncertain; the fragments survive only in catenae.
The original extent and structure of the commentary cannot be reconstructed from these excerpts.

_unresolved_facts.claim: urging them not to be held fast by the law
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: εὐκαίρως παραινῶν αὐτοῖς μὴ κρατεῖσθαι νόμῳ
_unresolved_facts.fix: timely exhorting them not to be held fast by the law (the source says Paul exhorts, not that Severian urges; this is Paul's action in the letter)

_unresolved_facts.claim: the Spirit intercedes for believers and enables spiritual requests free from fleshly elements
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα αὗται αἱ αἰτήσεις ἡμῶν μηδὲν ἔχωσι σαρκικόν. πνευματικὰς δὲ αἰτήσεις ἔχομεν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος βοηθουμένας
_unresolved_facts.fix: the Spirit intercedes for believers so that their requests may have nothing fleshly; they have spiritual requests helped by the power of the Spirit

_unresolved_facts.claim: u01-rem-early ... comments on the church as Christ's body and the fullness of God through Ephesians 2:14–15a
_unresolved_facts.fix: comments on the church as Christ's body and the fullness of God through Ephesians 1:22–23, then discusses the world, the devil as aerial spirit, and flesh/mind harmony in sin through Ephesians 2:2–3, and begins comment on the dividing wall at Ephesians 2:14–15a

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Eph 3,15 Ἐν οὐρανοῖς, φησίν, ἡ τῶν δικαίων διαγωγή, ἐπὶ γῆς δὲ ἡ πάντων ἀνθρώπων
_unresolved_facts.fix: through Ephesians 3:15, then continues with comments on the name of the Father coming from above, the cross as double, the church as fullness, spiritual songs, redeeming the time, the Eucharist, marriage as type, the Spirit's sword and intercession, and grace incorruptible through Ephesians 6:24

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐπισημαντέον δὲ ὅτι ἀφ' ὧν ὁ ἀπόστολος δείκνυσι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρός...
_unresolved_facts.fix: u01-rem-close begins with Ephesians 3:14-15 material (fatherhood, heavenly/earthly generations), then covers Ephesians 3:18-19 (cross dimensions), 5:14 (spiritual songs), 5:16 (redeeming time), 5:29 (Eucharist), 5:32-33 (marriage type), 6:17 (Spirit's sword), 6:18 (prayer in Spirit), 6:24 (grace), through Ephesians 6:24

_unresolved_facts.claim: John the Evangelist, whose prior preaching in Ephesus prepared the believers
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἰωάννου προλαβόντος καὶ τὸ κήρυγμα αὐτοῖς καταβαλλομένου
_unresolved_facts.fix: John, whose prior arrival and laying down of preaching prepared them (the source does not specify 'the Evangelist' here, though later at Eph 1:13 it asks if they heard from 'Ἰωάννου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ')

_unresolved_facts.claim: Quotations from Ephesians introduced by lemmata (Eph 1,1 etc.); Paul is referred to in third person
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: λέγει Παῦλος· ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης
_unresolved_facts.fix: Quotations from Ephesians introduced by lemmata; Paul is sometimes referred to in third person ('Paul says'), but the commentary also uses first-person exposition ('I already said beforehand')

_unresolved_facts.claim: Citations introduced by name (Ἰεζεκιὴλ, ∆αυίδ) or with ὁ θεός φησιν
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἣν οὖν εἶπε δόξαν ὁ Ἰεζεκιήλ, ταύτην ὁ θεός φησι τὸ ἐγώ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Citations introduced by name (Ἰεζεκιὴλ, ∆αυίδ), with ὁ θεός φησιν, or with formula 'this is what David says' (ὃ λέγει Δαυίδ)

_unresolved_facts.claim: One saying introduced with 'even if the Lord says' (κἂν ὁ κύριος λέγῃ)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: κἂν ὁ κύριος λέγῃ· εἶδον τὸν σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν πεσόντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: One saying introduced with 'even if the Lord says' (κἂν ὁ κύριος λέγῃ), but this is a counterfactual concession ('even if'), not a straightforward quotation; Severian then explains what the Lord meant
